turnover.verdict: No accuracy turnover exists inside {48,64,96}: accuracy rises monotonically 75.0 -> 81.3 -> 97.9 with every step outside the +/-4.17 pp band, and residual failures are abstentions shrinking 12 -> 9 -> 1. A cost turnover does exist and sits at C=48: prompt tokens are minimised there and rise 50.6% by C=96. The curves cross at C=48 — past it you pay more prompt tokens for more accuracy, and accuracy is still climbing at the top of the sweep.

evidence.cross_run_note: c48 bills 14679 here vs 15703 in E2 for byte-identical prompts (prompt_tokens match on every turn); the gap is prefix-cache warmth (turn 1 missed cache: 636 vs 124 billed, plus 20 turns hitting one 64-token block more). Cross-run billed comparisons are confounded by cache state; only within-run comparisons are valid. Prompt tokens are the cache-independent measure.

next_unit_hint: Accuracy is still rising at C=96 (47/48) and the only remaining failure is one abstention at the fixture's deepest probe (d32, turn 100). The sweep cannot see past d32 because TX-03's max distance is 32 — a turnover in accuracy, if it exists, needs either a fixture with deeper probes (TX-04 has d64) or C beyond 96. Cost is already rising 50.6% in prompt tokens by C=96 while billed stays nearly flat because of prefix caching, so the cost side of the trade is nearly free at these intervals; the binding constraint is the fixture's distance ceiling, not the budget (1927 requests of headroom remain).
